name: Invita Contracting - FAQ.pdf
extractedText:
INVITA / MAGELLAN CONTRACTING FAQ

=== CARRIERS ===

Carriers: Equitrust, Allianz, F&G, American Life, Delaware Life, Global Atlantic, Athene, North American, Corebridge, American Equity, Ibexis. All agents at street comp.

Roth Conversion carriers: Athene, North American, Equitrust, Allianz, American Equity, American Life.

Sub-agent carriers (below-street): Allianz (street/LOA only), Equitrust, American Equity, Athene, Nationwide Life, F&G.

Volume bonuses: Allianz and NOA increase comp at certain production thresholds.

=== TRANSFERS ===

Q: Will I lose access to my clients if I transfer?
A: If street to current FMO, no. If assigning comp to someone else, yes.

Q: Do I need a release?
A: Only if business written in last 6 months. Corebridge and American Equity don't require releases — writing code determines FMO credit.

Carrier-specific releases required: Sentinel, Aspida, GILICO, Global Atlantic, North American, Allianz (mark Preferred), Athene (needs GBS signature), American Life.

Q: Will my bonus transfer?
A: Allianz bonuses follow the agent. Others vary.

Q: Can I still service old FMO business?
A: Yes. Old business stays with old FMO. You keep visibility, servicing, and trail comp.

Q: Do I get overrides bringing agents to Invita?
A: No. All agents at street. No override option.

=== COMPENSATION ===

Q: Does Invita hold comp?
A: No. Carrier may hold 30 days on very large policies — rare.

LOA = Licensed-Only Agent. Carrier pays all comp to agency, not individual. Agency controls payout. Can be at or below street, never above.

Override = commission only, not book of business. Agent who signed the app keeps the client.

EQ and Delaware Life won't pay an individual into a business account.

=== CONTRACTING ISSUES ===

Q: Pending bankruptcy?
A: Can result in decline. Carriers generally require 24 months post-discharge. Harder if not due to divorce/illness.

Q: Outstanding VECTOR?
A: Equitrust/Athene: no (EQ requires 6mo after paid). F&G/Allianz: yes with payment plan. Corebridge: under $2k, max 2 hits. Case-by-case otherwise.

Q: Best Interest Training for non-resident states?
A: Only required for resident state. Exceptions: CA (8-hour), TX (4-hour).

Q: AML Training?
A: Federally required. Take at LIMRA (username=NPN, first password=lastname lowercase). Support: 866-364-2380. Corebridge requires completion within last 2 years.

Q: E&O insurance?
A: CNA or ACORD common. Shop at www.eoforless.com.

IGO checklist: verify state, training complete, E&O current, product training done.

=== BUSINESS STRUCTURE ===

Q: Can I set up an LLC with LOA?
A: Athene and F&G allow it. Comp goes to agency; agent handles 1099s/taxes.

Q: Two owners — who is principal?
A: Either. Must be signing officer on Articles of Incorporation.

Individual to business requires: Agency EIN, agency insurance license per state, voided business check, Articles of Incorporation, E&O listing agency name.

Sub-agent marketing credits: principal agent does NOT get credits for override amount.

=== SUBMITTING BUSINESS ===

Annuity e-apps: Magellan Firelight at https://www.firelighteapp.com/EGAccess/?org=MAG
Set up account 1-2 days before first submission. Product training required first.

Can skip Firelight and submit direct on carrier site — copy annuitybusiness@magellanfinancial.com.

Paper apps: email PDF to annuitybusiness@magellanfinancial.com or upload at https://www.partnerwithmagellan.com/annuity-secure-upload/

Life apps: contact Erica Cowger — ecowger@magellanfinancial.com or 866-779-3553. Use IGO for life e-apps (not Firelight).

Firelight trouble: use Chrome desktop, bookmark the MAG login link above, clear cookies if stuck, use separate emails if on multiple FMO platforms. Help: annuitybusiness@magellanfinancial.com

Annuity Rate Watch: https://members.annuityratewatch.com/invitafinancial/annuity/

=== TERMS ===

OBA=Outside Business Activity | LOE=Letter of Explanation | IGO=In Good Order | NIGO=Not In Good Order | LOA=Licensed-Only Agent | BD=Broker/Dealer

# Dinner & Movie Event FAQ

## What is this program?
The Retirement Everest Dinner & Movie program. Attendees get a free dinner and watch a movie (Retirement Deception, Social Insecurity, or License to Spend). After the movie, the advisor gives a short pitch and books appointments. Available movies rotate to keep messaging fresh.

## Why dinner? Can I just do refreshments?
No. Full meals drive maximum show-up rates. Think of it as a loss leader—you spend on food, you make it back many times over in closed business. Refreshments, coffee, and cookies will not produce the same results. Advisors who skip dinner get poor attendance and poor results.

## What are the target numbers?
Aim for ~30 attendees (~20-22 buying units). Goal is 50% of buying units book appointments—so 11+ appointments from 30 people. Advisors are writing $300K–$700K+ per event. Top producers: Jeremy Sparks wrote $1.5M in one week; Dustin wrote $4M in one month.

## Venue selection
Use a B to B-minus level restaurant with a private room (not fine dining, not Golden Corral). Examples: Red Lobster, Texas Roadhouse, nice Mexican or Italian restaurants. Theaters with kitchens also work. Buffet format—cheaper than plated, lets you control the environment. Target ~$30/plate. Start with restaurants (smaller, more interaction); scale to theaters/auditoriums later.

## When to hold events?
Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday nights work best. Lunch does not perform as well. Weekends are unproven. You can do two nights in the same week (e.g., Tue/Thu) and market to fill both. If your first night overfills, add a second night and backfill with digital.

## Marketing: digital vs. direct mail
Two options, use both. **Direct mail**: ~2x the cost of digital but higher quality leads and higher show-up rate. Contact Donnie (direct mail partner) for details. **Facebook ads**: Lower cost, uses a 3-filter process—exclusionary data uploads, targeted list (ages 55-74, with assets/income/home value filters), and trained Meta pixel. We target radius around the event, not zip codes. Ad creative should show the food and the offer. Rotate creative regularly.

## Lead confirmation process
Download the Lead Connector app. When a lead registers, immediately call or text to confirm. Ask how many are coming. Use the drip/confirmation emails in Producer Autopilot. Call/text the day before the event. This prevents over- or under-attendance. If enough people confirm early, tell remaining unconfirmed registrants the event is full—invite them to the next one.

## What if too many people show up?
Three options: (1) Turn them away—"We're full, come to our next event in two weeks," and give them a streaming card with your code so they can watch the movie at home. (2) Bring in more chairs and let them stay for the movie even if food runs out. (3) Have the restaurant bring more food.

## What if people eat and leave?
Don't worry about it. It happens occasionally but is not common. Those people were never going to convert anyway. Stay focused on the ones who stay—they're your real prospects.

## Event flow for Theaters only
1. **Guests arrive 15-20 min early** (dinner at 6:00, movie at 6:30). Staff member at the front door to guide people to the room.
2. **Buffet opens** — guests eat while watching the pre-roll trailer package.
3. **5 min before movie** — your assistant introduces you as the host.
4. **Opening pitch** — short, scripted (provided). Do NOT pitch during dinner or while food is being served.
5. **Movie plays.**
6. **Closing pitch** — short, scripted (provided). Do NOT open a Q&A or talk about annuity products/fees.
7. **Book appointments immediately** — staff hands out clipboards during the close. As each person finishes, a staff member is right there with a calendar to book one-on-one. Do NOT ask them to walk to the back of the room. Do NOT ask them to get up. Book them at their seat.
8. **After appointments are set**, you can mingle and chat.

## Event Flow for Restaurants Only
1. **Guests arrive 15-20 min early** (dinner at 6:00, movie at 6:30). Staff member at the front door to guide people to the room.
2. **Bread and salad on table**, eat something while watching the pre-roll trailer package.
3. **5 min before movie** — your assistant introduces you as the host.
4. **Opening pitch** — short, scripted (provided). Do NOT pitch during dinner or while food is being served.
5. **Movie plays.**
6. **Closing pitch** — short, scripted (provided). Do NOT open a Q&A or talk about annuity products/fees.
7. **Book appointments immediately** — staff hands out clipboards during the close. As each person finishes, a staff member is right there with a calendar to book one-on-one. Do NOT ask them to walk to the back of the room. Do NOT ask them to get up. Book them at their seat.
8. **Staff brings food and buffet** while everyone visits the restroom, etc.
9. **After appointments are set** you eat and mingle and chat.

## What is the sole goal of the event?
Appointments booked on the calendar. Not education, not Q&A, not a 20-minute slide presentation. One thing only: get appointments.

## Tech setup
Simple. Stream the movie from your phone or laptop. Options: venue's screen, your own projector (~$150 on Amazon), big-screen TV with HDMI, or laptop screen. **Critical**: use a powered/Bluetooth speaker—never play audio from laptop speakers. People forgive bad video; they will not forgive bad audio. Test audio beforehand from the back of the room.

## Opening & closing scripts
Use the provided scripts verbatim. They are built on psychology, proof, and hundreds of events. Do not ad-lib until you are writing $1M+/month. Practice and memorize them. Record yourself and get feedback if your appointment rate is below 50%.

## Where are the scripts?
The opening script, closing script, and first appointment script are on the members website under the Dinner and Movie section, in Sales Training.

## Photos
Take pictures at every event and send them in—they're used for additional marketing.
